body:
FROM THE P5 ERASURE LENS, 2026-08-19, on the T186 branch. The immediate false-report path is FIXED
on that branch — dropChannel now REFUSES rather than purging an empty in-memory copy and reporting a
completeness it never verified. What follows is what remains.

1. THE CLI SEVER VERB CANNOT SUCCEED ON THE HEALTHY PATH. resumeChannels fills attachedContainers
   but NOT federationChannels (the latter is written only by openChannelImpl). So a freshly booted
   process has no live channel handle, and re-opening throws "already attached here — drop() or
   detach() it first" (container.ts). `loam federate drop --channel X --yes` therefore exits 2 on
   exactly the stores where it is meant to work. The only path that returned 0 was the one that
   purged nothing, which is now refused. Net: the documented sever verb does not work. Fix by
   reaching the ATTACHED container rather than re-opening it.

2. THE CHANNEL RECORD SURVIVES ITS OWN DROP. dropChannelImpl purges the pool and clears the map, and
   never negates the CTX_CHANNEL status record. After a successful sever: `federate list` still
   prints the channel as receiving, setChannel still succeeds on it, and every later boot re-attempts
   an attach that cannot work because the declaration is struck. One command says severed and the
   next says standing. Curse records for the channel survive too.

3. AN UNATTACHED POOL SILENTLY LEAVES THE §11 FAN-OUT. resumeChannels catches and DISCARDS every
   attach failure. eraseImpl and erasureOutstanding enumerate tiers as gw.quarantinePools, which
   openSeparate populates only on a SUCCESSFUL attach. A channel pool holds a seeded copy of the
   primary's own deltas, so it is a real tier. Boot a store whose channel sqlite is locked or
   unreadable, then erase: the pool is not in the walk and the erasure reports complete while that
   file still holds the delta. Nothing reaches stderr either, unlike the mirror's purgeFailures,
   which this repo already routes to the operator. The bytes self-heal on the next successful attach
   (the settle path), but the report made in the meantime was false and unretractable — H7 with a
   silent swallow, H9's shape.

4. openChannel's IDEMPOTENCE SHORT-CIRCUIT DISCARDS THE CALLER'S ARGUMENTS. A second open with the
   same (into, prefix) returns the held channel and silently drops the new `source` and `bless`. The
   caller gets a channel that still pulls from the old source, with no signal. An operation with two
   outcomes must answer which one it was.

RAILS THE CURRENT SET CANNOT PROVIDE, and this is why all four survived: every drop rail drives
openChannel in-process over MemoryBackend with no channelBackend, so the map is always populated, the
pool has no file, and no CLI process boundary exists. NO TEST DROPS A SQLITE-BACKED CHANNEL, and no
test runs `federate drop` through the CLI. Add both.

TIER: the fixes are repairs (they make reports honest and a documented verb work) EXCEPT anything
that changes what gets purged — that is Myk's merge with its one-line statement.
title: Severing a channel: the CLI verb cannot succeed, and the record outlives the purge
